system: Krav Maga style belts and rank patches (IKMF-style layout)

sources.layout: Belt colours and patches follow the IKMF-style grading chart: White, Yellow, Orange, Green, Blue, Brown, Black belts; P (Practitioner, yellow patch), G (Graduate, cyan patch) and E (Expert, yellow patch with red letter, border and stripes). The number of stripes on a patch is the rank number. White carries a P patch with no stripes (P0); Yellow P1-P2; Orange P3-P4; Green P5 and G1; Blue G2-G3; Brown G4-G5; Black E1-E5.
sources.caveat: Aleph only borrows the look of the ladder. A rank here is Aleph's own: it means you finished every lesson in its range, in course order. It is not a Krav Maga grade, not an IKMF grade, and not an outside qualification. The gate sentences and the speed targets are Aleph's own proposals, not sourced.

trackNote: Ranks cover the Reading and prayer track only, in course order: r01-r51, then the 20 Intermediate reading lessons (I-01 to I-10, I-26 to I-35). The other 30 of the 50 I- lessons belong to the Israel track (Stage 3), which has no belts: it uses Stage 1, Stage 2 and Stage 3.

ranks.gate: Reads Shabbat Shalom: Shin, Bet, Tav, Lamed, final Mem and Vav with kamatz, patach, cholam and dagesh.
Meets the Priestly Blessing; Yod, Aleph, He, Resh and Mem with chirik and tzere.
Kaf, Nun and their finals; segol, the 'oo' vowels and shva.
About 19 letters including finals, 7 vowel signs, first decoded Priestly Blessing line.
All 27 letter shapes recognised; chataf vowels; Shema line 1 decoded.
Blessing formula fluent; shva, dagesh and stress rules applied.
All 15 signs plus exceptions (kamatz katan, prefixes, the Name).
Basic prayers: Shema, V'ahavta, Torah blessings, Modeh Ani, Mah Tovu, Kiddush.
Higher prayers: Avot, Mi Chamocha, Aleinu, Kaddish, Adon Olam, Birkat Hamazon opener.
Siddur page read inside a time limit.
Intermediate reading: the Shema and its blessings, Amidah openings, the Torah service and Kaddish responses.
Intermediate reading: Kiddush, Havdalah and the Hallel refrains.
Intermediate reading: Aleinu, Adon Olam and the blessings said for people.
Intermediate reading: the full Torah service, Shabbat-morning Amidah responses, Yom Kippur, Pesach and Sukkot.
Intermediate reading: Purim, Hanukkah, Birkat Hamazon openings, the journey blessings and Shabbat-day Kiddush.

wpmStatus: Every speed target is Aleph's own proposal, not sourced. Speed is never needed to earn a rank: ranks are earned by finishing lessons.
measurement: Words per minute on POINTED siddur text read aloud, errors subtracted (counted words read correctly / minutes). Self-reported on the Timed read screen; not measured by the app.
